answer.title: On stands: accelerate, brake, turn
answer.question: Do the actuators follow a command, the right way?
answer.passes: Every step of the stands run passes: the wheels reach each speed step up within 25 % (or 0.05 m/s), the steering tests give their numbers, and every fault tried is caught and the car still inside its limit (2 to 3 s).
answer.where: the Ravensim already running on this computer (attached, not started by the runner; ROS domain 97, this computer only), the car on stands

verdict.words: PASS: the wheels follow each speed step up (a step down is not judged); the steering follows its commands; 5 of 6 faults tried were caught in time (2 stopped the car by themselves; for 3 the watchdog named the lost sensor and the test stopped the car); NOT SHOWN: the front camera is lost. Not tried here: a Pi is lost: the camera Pi's link; a cable pulled.

graphs.title: The wheels: the speed asked for, and the speed measured
graphs.asks: Do the wheels follow a speed command?
graphs.from: step 4 (wheel-steps), its log.csv: cmd_speed (asked for), speed (measured); 885 samples
notes: 0.15: not measured, because it did not get 90 % of the way in the 4.0 s it had.

delay: the time until the measured line has moved 10 % of the way to the new value. 10 to 90 %: the time it then takes to get 90 % of the way. off at the end: the mean of the last quarter of the step, less the value asked for.
The log has a sample every 0.02 s: no time here is finer than that.
Asked for: what the test asks of the car (a speed). Measured: the speed the wheels report.

graphs.title: The steering: the angle asked for, and the angle measured
graphs.asks: Does the steering follow an angle command, the right way?
graphs.from: step 3a (steer-sweep), its log.csv: cmd_steer (asked for), steer (measured); 2286 samples
rows: off at the end, either way
facts: asked to the left (+), the measured angle went
to the left (+): the right way
notes: delay: the time until the measured line has moved 10 % of the way to the new value. 10 to 90 %: the time it then takes to get 90 % of the way. off at the end: the mean of the last quarter of the step, less the value asked for.

Asked for: the angle the test asks of the car.
graphs.judged: Step 3a (steer-sweep): PASS. Step 3b (steer-rate): PASS. Step 3c (steer-centre): PASS.

graphs.title: The brake: how hard it was asked to press, and how hard it did
graphs.asks: Does the brake follow its command?
graphs.from: step 4 (wheel-steps), its log.csv: brake_cmd (asked for), brake (measured); 885 samples
facts: asked to stop from 0.20 m/s, the wheels were still after
notes: delay: the time until the measured line has moved 10 % of the way to the new value. 10 to 90 %: the time it then takes to get 90 % of the way. off at the end: the mean of the last quarter of the step, less the value asked for.
The log has a sample every 0.02 s: no time here is finer than that.
Asked for: what the car's own software asks of the brake. The test asks for a speed; pressing the brake is the software's answer to 'stop'.
